:::{#def-subgroup-predictive-margin}

#### Exposed-subgroup predictive margin

The **exposed-subgroup predictive margin** averages the fitted risks
only over the observations actually exposed to $A = a$,
$S = \{i : A_i = a\}$,
and we give it its own symbol $\hat\pi_a(a)$:

$$
\hat\pi_a(a) \eqdef \frac{1}{n_a} \sum_{i : A_i = a} \hat\pi_{a,i}
$$

where $n_a$ is the number of observations with $A_i = a$.
The subscript records the treatment level the risks are predicted under,
and the argument records the subgroup averaged over;
the full-sample margin $\hat\pi_a$ averages over everyone instead.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-subgroup-pm}

#### Illustration: exposed-subgroup predictive margin

Continuing @exm-observed-marginal-risk,
where the exposed ($A = 1$) have
$\Pr(Z = 1 \mid A = 1) = `r round(p_z1_a1, 3)`$
and age-specific risks $\pi(1, 0) = `r round(pi1_z0, 3)`$
and $\pi(1, 1) = `r round(pi1_z1, 3)`$,
averaging the fitted risks over the exposed subgroup gives

$$
\hat\pi_1(1) = (1 - `r round(p_z1_a1, 3)`)(`r round(pi1_z0, 3)`)
+ (`r round(p_z1_a1, 3)`)(`r round(pi1_z1, 3)`)
= `r round((1 - p_z1_a1) * pi1_z0 + p_z1_a1 * pi1_z1, 3)`,
$$

which coincides with the [observed marginal risk](#def-observed-marginal-risk)
$\pi(1) = `r round(pi1_direct, 3)`$ (@exm-observed-marginal-risk),
not the [causal marginal risk](#def-causal-marginal-risk)
$\pi_1 = `r round((1 - p_z1_pop) * pi1_z0 + p_z1_pop * pi1_z1, 3)`$
(@exm-causal-marginal-risk);
@thm-subgroup-pm shows this agreement is no coincidence.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-subgroup-pm}

#### Exposed-subgroup predictive margin estimates the observed marginal risk

With the data $(Y_i, A_i, Z_i)$, $i = 1, \dots, n$, drawn [i.i.d.](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-iid) from the population,
under correct model specification,
and with the predictor vectors uniformly bounded
($\|x_{a,i}\| \le B < \infty$, as in @thm-g-computation-consistency),
the [exposed-subgroup predictive margin](#def-subgroup-predictive-margin) is consistent
for the observed marginal risk $\pi(a)$ (@def-observed-marginal-risk):

$$\hat\pi_a(a) \overset{p}{\to} \pi(a)$$

::: {.proof}

Split the [estimator](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/estimation.html#def-estimator) into the average of the **true** conditional risks
over the exposed subgroup plus an estimation-error term:

$$
\ba
\hat\pi_a(a)
&= \frac{1}{n_a} \sum_{i : A_i = a} \hat\pi(a, z_i)
&& \text{[definition of the estimator]}
\\
&= \frac{1}{n_a} \sum_{i : A_i = a} \teal{\pi(a, z_i)}
+ \frac{1}{n_a} \sum_{i : A_i = a} \paren{\hat\pi(a, z_i) - \teal{\pi(a, z_i)}}
&& \text{[add and subtract the true risks]}
\ea
$$

The estimation-error term converges to zero in probability
by the same bounded-predictor Lipschitz bound as in @thm-g-computation-consistency:
$\frac{1}{n_a}\sum_{i : A_i = a}\abs{\hat\pi(a, z_i) - \teal{\pi(a, z_i)}}
\le \tfrac{B}{4}\,\|\hat\beta - \beta^*\| \overset{p}{\to} 0$.
The observations with $A_i = a$ are an i.i.d. sample
from the conditional distribution $f_{Z \mid A}(z \mid a)$,
so the weak law of large numbers gives

$$
\frac{1}{n_a} \sum_{i : A_i = a} \teal{\pi(a, z_i)}
\overset{p}{\to} \E{\teal{\pi(a, Z)} \mid A = a}.
\qquad \text{[weak law of large numbers]}
$$

Finally, @thm-observed-marginal-risk identifies this [conditional expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-cond-expectation)
with the [observed marginal risk](#def-observed-marginal-risk):

$$
\E{\teal{\pi(a, Z)} \mid A = a} = \pi(a).
\qquad \text{[observed marginal risk theorem]}
$$

Combining the three steps, $\hat\pi_a(a) \overset{p}{\to} \pi(a)$.

:::

:::

The WCGS exposed-subgroup predictive margin from @exm-subgroup-pm
is therefore consistent for the observed marginal risk $\pi(1)$
by @thm-subgroup-pm.
